core_obligations: Reduce by Zariski localization (proof lines 6630-6632): since only a Zariski covering of V by schemes of the form U_Z with U etale over X is required, one may localize on X and on V, so it suffices to treat the case where X and V are affine.

Apply the affine lifting result (proof lines 6632-6633): in the affine case the cited result from Algebra produces the etale morphisms U_i -> X and the morphisms U_{i,Z} -> V whose images form a Zariski covering of V.
Conclude (statement with the proof): the resulting family {U_{i,Z} -> V} is the required Zariski covering of V by restrictions of etale morphisms to X.
proof_roadmap: Observe that the assertion is Zariski local on X and on V.
Reduce to X and V affine.
Apply the standard lifting of etale morphisms along a closed immersion over an affine base.
Read off the required Zariski covering of V.
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces a Zariski covering of an etale Z-scheme V by restrictions of etale X-schemes along a closed immersion i : Z -> X (statement lines 6620-6627). The proof is a localization reduction: because the conclusion only asks for a Zariski covering, one may localize on X and V and thereby assume both affine (proof lines 6630-6632), after which the affine case is exactly the cited lifting result from the chapter Algebra (proof lines 6632-6633). The content is the recognition that the assertion is Zariski local, which is what licenses the reduction to the affine situation. The claim is H2: one localisation reduction plus one cited affine statement.
